blocks.title: Possible explanations

paragraphs.text: **The school department’s written answer to the Town Manager’s 1 September request about the reclassification.** It would say whether the district stands by the entry and, if not, why.

Behind it: any correcting entry after 6 October, or a rerun of the period-13 reports; the Town Accountant’s fund 2640 balances at 30 June 2025 and 2026; the “FY26 problems worksheet”; the signed original of batch 5853.

**Allowed.** State law lets a school committee approve paying up to three months of tuition in advance (G.L. c. 71, s. 71D), and the state’s Division of Local Services uses this case as its example: a July to September bill, due 30 June, charged to the year that is ending.

**Not announced.** Every June and July 2026 meeting of the School Committee, Finance Committee and Select Board was read, minutes and recordings. None mentions this payment or the re-charge to the circuit breaker. No minutes record an advance-tuition vote. The warrant for the last two weeks of June was on the School Committee’s 15 July agenda and is in that meeting’s minutes with no motion or vote; the Chair wrote on 27 October that no vote was taken. No later agenda or minutes lists it.

**Not presented, on any record we hold.** The payment is batch 5853. The district says the 15 July warrant was its batches to 30 June; the nine delivered do not include 5853. The 29 July warrant, 6 to 20 July, is $100,507.91 in all, less than the batch. No agenda, minutes or recording names the batch, check 218995 or the invoices. The copy the district supplied on 19 November 2026 has blank signature lines, and the district says the signed originals “were immediately sent to Town Hall for processing and signature by the SelectBoard.”
**Not yet held.** The signed original of batch 5853, and the School Committee’s September year-end budget reviews. Each is a registered gap, listed on What we cannot answer.
